text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Turkish President Suleiman Demirel will visit Estonia on June 3-4.
- The people of Abkhasia have asked for the government's help to be able to maintain Estonian-language education there.
- Transport minister Raivo Vare stressed that the "Estonia" disaster investigation commission must continue and complete its work. He rejected the calls for a new commission.
- The Tallinn bourse will stop trading Saku Brewery shares, because the company has refused to reveal its first quarter results.
- Parliament has decided to publish a synopsis of the audit made in the Bank of Estonia and to invalidate the resolution handing over $150 million worth of forest plots to the bank to back the kroon.
- The government will decide whether or not to raise the maximum speed limit to 100 kilometres per hour this summer.
- Priit Kelder, director of the Estonian national bureau of interpol, agreed to become interior ministry vice-chancellor.
- Former fleet director of the fishery firm Ookean, Aksel Siimer, has been charged with the loss of 23 million kroons by selling the state's ships at bargain prices.
- The Tartu city court has prohibited the dismissal of foreign students from the university following their refusal to pay the unexpectedly increased tuition fee.
- The central bank reiterated its assurances of the stability of the kroon following the devaluation of the Czech national currency.
